note: zForth (Ico Doornekamp / zevv), a tiny embeddable Forth — a small C VM plus a Forth-source bootstrap (forth/core.zf) that defines the language — cross-compiled to a 16-bit MS-DOS MZ .EXE with ia16-elf-gcc. It is DOS-NATIVE: it runs on the bw-board 8086 DOS service bench, reads PROG.FTH via INT 21h, and prints via the C library. dosmain.c embeds forth/core.zf (the language only; the stock misc.zf FizzBuzz demo and memaccess.zf load-time asserts are excluded), evaluates it, prints a banner, then reads and evaluates PROG.FTH. Packaged as media-lab project projects/forth-dos (fetch.sh reproduces this byte-for-byte). zf_cell is float, so the build uses the medium model (soft-float %g), like fe.exe. Build tool ia16-elf-gcc is GPL but build-time only; the binary links permissive newlib + libi86.
